title: A Critique of Master Huijing's Pure Land School Charter
author: Zhanran
excerpt: Q: Master Huijing (for his background, see What Is the Original Vow School?) laid down the Pure Land School Charter, whose editor's note says: "The Charter is the general outline of the doctrine of one school (the Pure Land school) and the standard that practitioners follow; its importance to the school is like that of a nation's constitution." Is this so?

inline.s: Q: Master Huijing (for his background, see
What Is the Original Vow School?

) laid down the Pure Land School Charter, whose editor's note says: "The Charter is the general outline of the doctrine of one school (the Pure Land school) and the standard that practitioners follow; its importance to the school is like that of a nation's constitution." Is this so?

A: This Pure Land School Charter abounds in errors. Master Huijing himself has not attained even the most elementary one-pointedness of mind, to say nothing of realizing the samādhi of Buddha-recitation! A man of no cultivation whatever, who cannot even speak of the realm of realization, boldly assumes the rank of a patriarch of the Pure Land school and, with his deluded consciousness, fabricates at random "the general outline of the doctrine of one school (the Pure Land school) and the standard that practitioners follow" — truly he does not know the height of heaven or the depth of earth, and passes himself off as a sage! A man who trumpets "the evil person is the true recipient" (and therefore no need to keep the precepts) and "calling the Name guarantees rebirth" (and therefore no need to cultivate), a man who can do nothing but wag his tongue, presumes to lay down a "standard to be followed" for every practitioner of the entire Pure Land school, and to have it followed as though it were a constitution! Followed in what? Followed in the non-observance of precepts and the absence of cultivation that they trumpet?

[Trumpeting "the evil person is the true recipient" and "calling the Name guarantees rebirth"] In his The Essential Meaning of Master Shandao, Master Huijing says: "They do not know that the purpose of the Contemplation Sūtra is to reveal Amitābha's original vow: the evil person is the true recipient." Master Huijing's refuge disciple, Master Xinyuan, says: "Let us now look at Amitābha Buddha's deliverance: for what kind of living being is it intended, who is the true recipient? The evil person is the true recipient." Master Huijing's compilation, the
Dharma Words of Master Hōnen (also titled Dharma Words on Buddha-Recitation and Peace of Mind), says: "The Pure Land school's
essential point
lies in this: no matter who one may be, whoever recites the Buddha is reborn.
Though there be an evil person in the world without
equal (nothing comparable) —
even such a one,
if he recites Namo Amitābha Buddha,
even a single thought brings rebirth

." It also says: "If a person commits the five heinous crimes and hears the six-character Name (hears 'Namo Amitābha Buddha'), the fiery cart departs of itself (the fiery cart of hell departs of itself), and the lotus throne comes at once to welcome him." [Five heinous crimes] The five heinous offenses: the five offenses most utterly contrary to principle, namely patricide, matricide, killing an arhat, shedding the Buddha's blood, and causing schism in the Saṅgha. These five are acts of extreme evil; whoever commits any one of them falls into the Avīci Hell, and so they are also called 'unintermitted karma.'
What is more, the Buddha said we must
cultivate in accordance with the Dharma
(see The Buddha Speaks the Sūtra of Immeasurable Life), and we must
cultivate in accordance with the teaching
(see
Commentary on the Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha in Praise of the Pure Land and the Buddhas' Protection

), does Master Huijing know what cultivation is? He has not the least bit of skill, not even the outermost hairs of it; by what virtue or ability does he presume, in the role of a Pure Land patriarch, to instruct living beings! It is enough to make one's teeth fall out laughing. Only in the Original Vow school could there be such a brazen and demented person!
[Cultivating in accordance with the Dharma] In The Buddha Speaks the Sūtra of Immeasurable Life, the Buddha says:
"Therefore my Dharma is thus practiced, thus spoken, thus taught. You should believe and comply, and cultivate in accordance with the Dharma."

[Cultivating in accordance with the teaching] In The Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha in Praise of the Pure Land and the Buddhas' Protection, the World-Honored One repeatedly and again and again stresses the need to
cultivate in accordance with the teaching

, and declares plainly that whoever cultivates in accordance with the teaching is embraced by the Buddhas of the ten directions, is certain to be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, will never retreat, and will quickly realize Buddhahood:

"If there are good men or good women of pure faith who hear the name of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, possessed of inconceivable merit, and of the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss, all of them should believe and accept and make the vow,
cultivating in accordance with the teaching
, and be born in that Buddha-land."
Those who cultivate in accordance with the teaching

are all certain to attain anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi and become irreversible; all are certain to be born in the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life. Therefore, Śāriputra, all you sentient beings should
believe, accept, and comprehend the words of myself and of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones of the ten directions
, and strive with diligence,
cultivating in accordance with the teaching
, and harbor no doubt."
Those who cultivate in accordance with the teaching

are all certain to attain anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi and become irreversible; all are certain to be born in the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life. Therefore, Śāriputra, if there are good men or good women of pure faith, they should all, with profound minds, believe and understand the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Ultimate Bliss of Immeasurable Life, make the vow to be born there,
and not act with heedlessness

"In this defiled Sahā world, in an evil age of the five turbidities, if there are good men or good women of pure faith who hear this teaching, the most difficult of all in the world to believe, and can give rise to faith and understanding, uphold it, and expound it,
cultivating in accordance with the teaching

, you should know that such a person is most rare, and has planted roots of goodness before countless Buddhas. When such a person's life ends, he will certainly be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss and enjoy the Mahāyāna bliss of the pure Buddha-land adorned with all manner of merits."

Q: The Pure Land School Charter drawn up by Master Huijing establishes Master Shandao as the school's patriarch, with the lineage: Nāgārjuna Bodhisattva, Vasubandhu Bodhisattva, Master Tanluan, Master Daochuo, Master Shandao. Do they truly revere Nāgārjuna Bodhisattva, Vasubandhu Bodhisattva, Master Tanluan, Master Daochuo, and Master Shandao?

A: The lineage of the Pure Land school in our country is the thirteen patriarchs beginning with Master Huiyuan: Huiyuan, Shandao, Chengyuan, Fazhao, Shaokang, Yanshou, Shengchang, Lianchi, Ouyi, Jieliu, Sheng'an, Chewu, Yinguang, and the rest. The Japanese Original Vow school (the True Pure Land school), however, takes India's Nāgārjuna Bodhisattva and Vasubandhu Bodhisattva, China's Master Tanluan, Chan Master Daochuo, and Master Shandao, and Japan's Genshin Sōzu and Master Hōnen as patriarchs of the Pure Land school, calling them the "seven patriarchs of three countries." Some years ago Huijing, Jingzong, and others loudly promoted the "seven patriarchs of three countries" and clamored that the great edifice of China's Pure Land school
must "have its pillars replaced,"

establishing the "seven patriarchs of three countries" as its lineage, in a vain attempt to replace the orthodox Chinese Pure Land school of a thousand years with the Original Vow school. Later, because Master Hōnen had been thoroughly discredited, they no longer dared to propose Master Hōnen as a patriarch of the Chinese Pure Land school, and so they vainly attempted to take the first five of the "seven patriarchs of three countries" — Nāgārjuna Bodhisattva, Vasubandhu Bodhisattva, Master Tanluan, Master Daochuo, and Master Shandao — as the lineage of the Chinese Pure Land school, replacing the original lineage of thirteen patriarchs.

In reality, they do not truly revere Nāgārjuna Bodhisattva, Vasubandhu Bodhisattva, Master Tanluan, Master Daochuo, and Master Shandao at all; they mean to use them to repudiate the tradition of the Chinese Pure Land school and to put the Original Vow school in its place.

blocks.text: 1. Huijing, Jingzong, and Others Pay Lip Service While Doing the Opposite

inline.s: Let us now look in concrete terms at whether they truly revere
Nāgārjuna Bodhisattva, Vasubandhu Bodhisattva, Master Tanluan, Master Daochuo, and Master Shandao:

Nāgārjuna Bodhisattva devoted his life to promoting the doctrine of the Middle Way and the emptiness of intrinsic nature. His writings were exceedingly abundant; the number of treatises he composed is rarely matched in the world, and he is honored with the fine title "master of a thousand treatises." Later generations, basing themselves on his Treatise on the Middle Way, propagated the doctrine of the Middle Way and the emptiness of intrinsic nature, calling it the Madhyamaka school and honoring Nāgārjuna Bodhisattva as its founder. Huijing, Jingzong, and others understand nothing whatever of the doctrine of the Middle Way and the emptiness of intrinsic nature; their statements run entirely counter to it.
How can they be said to revere Nāgārjuna Bodhisattva?
In his Treatise on Rebirth, Vasubandhu Bodhisattva declares (see
Commentary on the Treatise on Rebirth
World-Honored One, with
one mind
(thought succeeding thought without interruption, with no other thought intermingled)
, I take refuge in the Unobstructed Light Tathāgata who fills the ten directions
(Amitābha Buddha)
, and vow to be born in the Land of Peace and Bliss
(the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss)
With the mind ever making the vow,
with one mind
and exclusive mindfulness
, one is ultimately born in the land of Peace and Bliss, because one wishes
to cultivate śamatha in accordance with reality
(calm abiding)
[One mind]
Master Tanluan comments in his Commentary on the Treatise on Rebirth:
My
one mind
is Vasubandhu Bodhisattva's word of self-admonition. It means being mindful of the Unobstructed Light Tathāgata and vowing to be born in the Land of Peace and Bliss,
thought succeeding thought without interruption, with no other thought intermingled

Thus "one mind" means thought succeeding thought without interruption, with no other thought intermingled. [Taking refuge] The Sanskrit word is namas, rendered in Chinese as "taking refuge"; it is the utterance of living beings who take refuge in the Buddha with utmost sincerity and believe and comply.

[Unobstructed Light Tathāgata] One of the honored epithets of Amitābha Buddha's light. Amitābha Buddha has twelve honored epithets of light: Buddha of Immeasurable Light, Buddha of Boundless Light, Buddha of Unobstructed Light, Buddha of Unopposed Light, Buddha of Blazing King Light, Buddha of Pure Light, Buddha of Joyous Light, Buddha of Wisdom Light, Buddha of Uninterrupted Light, Buddha of Inconceivable Light, Buddha of Ineffable Light, Buddha of Light Surpassing the Sun and Moon.

[Taking refuge in the Unobstructed Light Tathāgata who fills the ten directions] Taking refuge in the Unobstructed Light Tathāgata whose light illumines all the lands of the ten directions — that is, taking refuge in Amitābha Buddha, whose light shines universally over the lands of the ten directions. The Buddha Speaks the Amitābha Sūtra says:
"The light of that Buddha is immeasurable and illumines the lands of the ten directions without obstruction; therefore he is called Amitābha."
[Śamatha] Rendered in Chinese as "calm abiding." Calm abiding means
stilling all distracting thoughts.
Vasubandhu Bodhisattva teaches us to be of
one mind
thought succeeding thought without interruption, with no other thought intermingled)
, to be
single-mindedly and exclusively mindful
, and to
cultivate calm abiding in accordance with reality
(śamatha)
. This is the key to rebirth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Yet Huijing, Jingzong, and others loudly trumpet Buddha-recitation with a scattered mind and the slogan "calling the Name guarantees rebirth."
How can they be said to revere Vasubandhu Bodhisattva?

Master Tanluan was a sage who had realized the fruit. He too spoke with perfect clarity on how one may be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss. In his Commentary on the Treatise on Rebirth and his Brief Discussion of the Meaning of the Pure Land of Peace and Bliss, Master Tanluan declares
(see
Master Tanluan's Pure Land Teaching
One mind means thought succeeding thought without interruption, with no other thought intermingled.
With no other thought intermingled, thought following thought in succession
(in unbroken sequence)
, even down to ten thoughts, this is called the continuity of ten thoughts.
If ten thoughts continue without interruption at the moment of death, one attains rebirth.
Yet Huijing, Jingzong, and others loudly trumpet
calling the Name guarantees rebirth
which stands in direct opposition to Master Tanluan's teaching. How can they be said to revere Master Tanluan?

Master Daochuo was a sage who had realized the fruit. He too spoke with perfect clarity on how one may be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss. In his Collection on the Land of Peace and Bliss, Master Daochuo declares
(see
Master Daochuo's Pure Land Teaching
If there are living beings who, though they have done evil all their lives,
at the moment of death have ten thoughts in unbroken succession
, call my name,
then if they are not born there, may I not attain perfect enlightenment.
Yet Huijing, Jingzong, and others loudly trumpet
calling the Name guarantees rebirth
which stands in direct opposition to Master Daochuo's teaching. How can they be said to revere Master Daochuo?
Master Shandao was Amitābha Buddha come again. He spoke with perfect clarity on how one may be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss. Master Shandao declares
(see
Master Shandao's Pure Land Teaching
Precisely because calling the Name is easy,
continuity brings rebirth
. If one can
continue thought after thought
persevering to the end of one's life
then ten out of ten are born, a hundred out of a hundred are born.
I pray that all people reflect well on this: whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, one must
brace the mind and master oneself
(spur oneself on and restrain oneself)
never ceasing day or night
(never ceasing, day or night, the continuity of thought after thought)
— the former thought is the end of this life, the latter thought is rebirth. To enjoy forever the bliss of the Unconditioned Dharma, and at the last to attain Buddhahood: is that not a joy indeed!

Since the Pure Land School Charter establishes Master Shandao as the school's patriarch, the whole Charter ought to carry through Master Shandao's teaching; yet the Charter not only lacks the exceedingly important declaration above, it does not even contain
"continuity brings rebirth"
— not even these few words!
How can this be called honoring Master Shandao as the school's patriarch?
Moreover, Huijing, Jingzong, and others loudly trumpet
calling the Name guarantees rebirth
and
the evil person is the true recipient
(see
Does Calling the Name Guarantee Rebirth?
What Is the Original Vow School?
and
The Original Vow School Is a Non-Buddhist Sect Attached to Buddhism

), and slanderously claim that this is "Amitābha's original vow." In his The Essential Meaning of Master Shandao, Master Huijing says: "They do not know that the purpose of the Contemplation Sūtra is to
reveal Amitābha's original vow
: the evil person is the true recipient."
This stands in direct opposition to Master Shandao's teaching

(Master Shandao says continuity brings rebirth, while Master Huijing says calling the Name guarantees rebirth; Master Shandao says one must brace the mind and master oneself, while Master Huijing says the evil person is the true recipient)
. How can they be said to revere Master Shandao?

blocks.text: 2. The "Essential Point of the Pure Land School" That Huijing, Jingzong, and Others Trumpet

inline.s: From the Complete Works of Master Hōnen, Master Huijing carefully picked
out
forty-eight sayings — in the Forty-Eight Dharma Words of Master Hōnen (also titled Dharma Words on Buddha-Recitation and Peace of Mind) there are the following two passages (see
A Critique of the Dharma Words on Buddha-Recitation and Peace of Mind
The Pure Land school's
essential point
is this: no matter who one may be, whoever recites the Buddha is reborn. Though there be an evil person in the world without
equal (nothing comparable) —
even such a one, if he recites Namo Amitābha Buddha, even a single thought brings rebirth."
If a person commits the five heinous crimes

(the five heinous offenses: the five offenses most utterly contrary to principle, namely patricide, matricide, killing an arhat, shedding the Buddha's blood, and causing schism in the Saṅgha. These five are acts of extreme evil; whoever commits any one of them falls into the Avīci Hell, and so they are also called 'unintermitted karma')
, and hears the six-character Name
(hears 'Namo Amitābha Buddha')
the fiery cart departs of itself
(the fiery cart of hell departs of itself)
, and the lotus throne comes at once to welcome him."
In these two "declarations," Master Hōnen gives the essential point of the Original Vow school —
calling the Name guarantees rebirth
(indeed, even hearing the Name guarantees rebirth) and
the evil person being the true recipient
— its most vivid and complete expression; Huijing, Jingzong, and others hold it in the highest esteem and proclaim it far and wide. How
can this be called revering Master Tanluan, Master Daochuo, and Master Shandao?
"Calling the Name guarantees rebirth"
and
"the evil person is the true recipient"
— these two principles are the Original Vow school's
essential point
They cleverly exploit the weaknesses of human nature — the fear of hardship, the wish for shortcuts, the craving for worldly pleasures — in order to deceive the faithful.

"Calling the Name guarantees rebirth" is the theoretical justification for monastics not to cultivate; "the evil person is the true recipient" is the theoretical justification for monastics not to keep the precepts and not to abandon evil and practice good. And so monastics degenerate from cultivators of the Way into professional monks who neither keep the precepts nor cultivate: they grow their hair, eat meat, take wives, do evil — anything at all. The tragedy is that they still believe they will certainly be reborn, because they have "calling the Name guarantees rebirth" and "the evil person is the true recipient" as their guarantee — never realizing that these are nothing but lying nonsense! See
The Original Vow School Is a Non-Buddhist Sect Attached to Buddhism
and
The Practice of Master Hōnen's Teaching
"Calling the Name guarantees rebirth" and "the evil person is the true recipient"
— these two principles are the essential point of the Original Vow school.] These are Master Hōnen's own words. Hōnen says:
The Pure Land school's
essential point
is this: no matter who one may be, whoever recites the Buddha is reborn.
Though there be an evil person in the world without
equal (nothing comparable) —
even such a one,
if he recites Namo Amitābha Buddha,
even a single thought brings rebirth
In The Buddha Speaks the Amitābha Sūtra, the Buddha says:
"One cannot be born in that land with few roots of goodness, blessings, and causes."
Yet Huijing, Jingzong, and others loudly trumpet
the evil person is the true recipient
(see
The Original Vow School Is a Non-Buddhist Sect Attached to Buddhism

), and slanderously claim that this is "Amitābha's original vow." In his The Essential Meaning of Master Shandao, Master Huijing says: "They do not know that the purpose of the Contemplation Sūtra is to
reveal Amitābha's original vow
: the evil person is the true recipient."

blocks.text: 3. Huijing, Jingzong, and Others Mislead Living Beings on the Core Question of Rebirth

inline.s: Let us look next at what Huijing, Jingzong, and others, on
"how one may attain rebirth"
, this
core question
of the Pure Land school,
are trumpeting, and how they mislead the faithful
On "how one may attain rebirth," Master Tanluan, Master Daochuo, and Master Shandao all gave clear declarations
On how one may be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss,
Master Tanluan spoke with perfect clarity; in his Commentary on the Treatise on Rebirth and his Brief Discussion of the Meaning of the Pure Land of Peace and Bliss he declares
(see
Master Tanluan's Pure Land Teaching
Master Daochuo also spoke with perfect clarity on how one may be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss
; in his Collection on the Land of Peace and Bliss he declares
(see
Master Daochuo's Pure Land Teaching
On how
one may be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss
, Amitābha Buddha come again, Master Shandao, likewise spoke with perfect clarity
(see
Master Shandao's Pure Land Teaching
[Continuity brings rebirth]
At the moment of death, one need only keep the thought of Buddha-recitation continuous (uninterrupted by deluded thoughts) to attain rebirth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Concerning
ten thoughts at the moment of death: continuity brings rebirth
," Master Shandao declares:

If I attain Buddhahood and the living beings of the ten directions call my name, vow to be born in my land, and do so even down to ten thoughts, then if they are not born there, may I not attain perfect enlightenment.
" (The Four-Part Commentary on the Contemplation Sūtra)

If I attain Buddhahood and the living beings of the ten directions vow to be born in my land and call my name even down to ten utterances, then by the power of my vow, if they are not born there, may I not attain perfect enlightenment.
(The Gate of Contemplation and Recitation)
If I attain Buddhahood and the living beings of the ten directions call my name even down to ten utterances, then if they are not born there, may I not attain perfect enlightenment.
Hymns of Praise for Rebirth)
When the phrases "even down to ten thoughts" and "even down to ten utterances" used here are read together with Master Shandao's declaration above —
"Precisely because calling the Name is easy, continuity brings rebirth. If one can
continue thought after thought, persevering to the end of one's life
, then ten out of ten are born, a hundred out of a hundred are born" —
it becomes obvious that this is an abbreviated way of saying "from the whole of one's life (a lifetime) down to
ten thoughts continued at the moment of death
," for Master Shandao has already said plainly:
"Continue thought after thought, persevering to the end of one's life."
And
"continue thought after thought, persevering to the end of one's life"
is precisely in order to make the continuity of thought after thought second nature through habit,
so as to ensure ten continuous thoughts at the moment of death
If one does not recite the Buddha at the moment of death, or recites with a scattered mind at the moment of death, then it is not
"continue thought after thought, persevering to the end of one's life"
Therefore
"even down to ten thoughts; if they are not born, may I not attain perfect enlightenment"
means:
ten thoughts at the moment of death; continuity brings rebirth.
[Ten thoughts, ten utterances] Reciting the Buddha's Name ten times.
[The continuity of thought after thought becoming second nature through habit] Through constant repeated practice, making the continuity of thought after thought a matter of instinct.

Master Shandao was Amitābha Buddha come again; his words are Amitābha Buddha's words. On how one may attain rebirth, we must of course take his words as our authority! Those who recite the Buddha's Name must engrave this on their hearts, believing yet more deeply and trusting yet more firmly.
Yet on how one may be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss,
the Original Vow school's
essential point
is
calling the Name guarantees rebirth
(indeed, even hearing the Name guarantees rebirth) and
the evil person being the true recipient
. This too is what Huijing, Jingzong, and others proclaim far and wide. For example:
If a person commits the five heinous crimes

(the five heinous offenses: the five offenses most utterly contrary to principle, namely patricide, matricide, killing an arhat, shedding the Buddha's blood, and causing schism in the Saṅgha. These five are acts of extreme evil; whoever commits any one of them falls into the Avīci Hell, and so they are also called 'unintermitted karma')
, and hears the six-character Name
(hears 'Namo Amitābha Buddha')
the fiery cart departs of itself
(the fiery cart of hell departs of itself)
, and the lotus throne comes at once to welcome him."
This means:
a great evildoer who has committed the five heinous crimes need only hear the Buddha's Name
(without even reciting it)
and is at once reborn.

blocks.text: 4. Huijing, Jingzong, and Others Seek to Usurp the Chinese Pure Land School with the Original Vow School

inline.s: When the fallacious and heretical doctrines that Huijing, Jingzong, and others proclaim far and wide are set beside the declarations of Vasubandhu Bodhisattva, Master Tanluan, Master Daochuo, and Master Shandao, it becomes clear that the reliance they profess on Master Tanluan, Master Daochuo, and Master Shandao, and their claim to a lineage running through Nāgārjuna Bodhisattva, Vasubandhu Bodhisattva, Master Tanluan, Master Daochuo, and Master Shandao, are nothing but a front; behind the scenes they are promoting the Original Vow school, in a vain attempt to replace the Chinese Pure Land tradition, whose first patriarch is Master Huiyuan, with the Original Vow school.

Their drafting of the Pure Land School Charter and a whole series of conspiratorial undertakings amounts to usurping the Chinese Pure Land school and replacing the true Dharma with a heretical teaching
(see
The Original Vow School Is a Non-Buddhist Sect Attached to Buddhism
! The karmic cause and effect of such deeds is a fall into the Avīci Hell. I earnestly urge Huijing, Jingzong, and others, together with their followers, to think thrice before they act!

blocks.text: 5. Huijing, Jingzong, and Others Peddle Fake Medicine

inline.s: The most despicable and odious thing in the world is to sell fake medicine — to ruin people's lives for the sake of a few coins. That bit of money is utterly insignificant beside a human life, which is a matter of supreme consequence. For such petty gain they take on the debt of many human lives, a debt that must be repaid life after life!

Huijing, Jingzong, and others are all the more despicable and odious: they peddle fake medicine in the Dharma itself! It is simply that they have no true cultivation of their own, yet wish to scoop up a little fame and profit (and that fame and profit is utterly insignificant beside the wisdom-life of those who recite the Buddha's Name), and so, heedless of the wisdom-life of Buddha-reciters, they peddle their fake medicine far and wide:
calling the Name guarantees rebirth
the evil person is the true recipient

, and so on. Do they never consider what kind of life-debt they incur, what kind of evil karma they create, what kind of evil retribution they will receive! Is that little bit of fame and profit worth it? Will the theory that "the evil person is the true recipient" save you?
The Buddha says:
"Therefore you should know that such a person would rather cut out his own tongue with a sharp knife than speak impure Dharma amid the assembly."
Translation: such a person would rather cut off his own tongue with a sharp knife than speak impure Dharma amid the assembly.)
(The Buddha Treasury Sūtra)
Because the retribution of speaking impure Dharma is so terrible, the Buddha says:
"If a person were to take the lives of all living beings in the three thousand great thousand worlds, the offense of speaking impure Dharma would be greater than that."
(Translation: if someone were to take the lives of all living beings in the three thousand great thousand worlds, the offense of speaking impure Dharma would be greater still.)
(The Buddha Treasury Sūtra)
[Blatantly peddling counterfeit medicine] Comparing what Huijing, Jingzong and the like so loudly trumpet —
recitation of the Name surely brings rebirth
and
the evil man as the true vessel

— with the instruction of the Bodhisattva Vasubandhu, Master Tanluan, Master Daochuo, and Master Shandao set forth above, whether it is true or false is clear at a glance. The reason Huijing, Jingzong and others dare not teach the true Dharma is that they themselves have no genuine practice. If they were to teach that wholehearted Buddha-recitation means reciting with no stray thoughts, or that thought follows thought unbroken, or that this unbroken mindfulness is in itself rebirth, then the faithful would ask them: How is this to be accomplished? Have you accomplished it yourselves? How could they possibly answer! And so they sell counterfeit medicine to deceive and mislead.
[Unclean preaching] Preaching with a defiled mind for the sake of fame, gain, and the like, or preaching without rightly comprehending the meaning of the Buddhadharma.
Thus it is said:
Past the sunken boat a thousand sails are streaming,
Before the blighted tree ten thousand greens are teeming.
